root_cause.text: The ice driver incorrectly set the XDP RxQ frag_size field to the DMA write length (partial buffer size) instead of the full buffer size (truesize/frame_sz), causing bpf_xdp_frags_increase_tail() to compute negative tailroom and trigger a kernel panic.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "the only user of frag_size field in XDP RxQ info is bpf_xdp_frags_increase_tail(). It clearly expects whole buff size instead of DMA write size. Different assumptions in ice driver configuration lead to negative tailroom." The patch changes the assignment from `ring->rx_buf_len` to `ring->truesize` for non-ZC mode and from `xsk_pool_get_rx_frame_size` to `xsk_pool_get_rx_frag_step` for ZC mode.

The conditional check for previous errors, though not directly assigning frag_size, is part of the code path that leads to the vulnerable xsk_pool_set_rxq_info call when ring->xsk_pool is set.
